image_description: A ferret (Mustela putorius furo) with dark brown/black guard hairs and a lighter cream/white undercoat is resting on top of a dark blue backpack. The animal has an elongated body, short legs, and a bushy tail. It is positioned in the center of the frame, lying on the bag which sits on a concrete surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Small triangular head with pointed snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The subject displays a distinct mustelid head shape with a tapered, pointed snout and triangular profile, consistent with the taxonomy.
Visible eye is small, dark, and bead-like, matching the description.
Ears are low-set, short, and rounded, barely protruding from the fur/head shape.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Extremely elongated slender body with remarkably fine, diminutive proportions and lightweight build.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body is visibly long and tubular relative to its height, characteristic of the weasel family.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Short dense fur in brown dorsally with white or yellow ventral coloration.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal fur is dark brown/black, transitioning to a lighter cream/white on the sides and underside (ventral), matching the 'sable' or standard ferret coloration.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Some species turn white in winter (ermine morph).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a conditional seasonal trait. The current image shows a non-white morph, so this specific checkpoint is not applicable/testable for this instance.
The neck appears long and flexible, connecting the head smoothly to the torso.
The visible forelimb is short and tucked under the body, consistent with the anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Short tail relative to body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear; while bushy, it is significantly shorter than the main body trunk.
